overview:
Compact flagships are rare, and this one refuses to compromise on power to stay small. Xiaomi sells the 12GB RAM, 512GB storage version in Pakistan at an official price of Rs 269,999 through mistore.pk, with market listings at the same figure, so you are paying top-tier money for a handset that still fits one hand. Its 6.36-inch LTPO AMOLED screen runs at 120Hz, which keeps scrolling fluid while the LTPO tech lets the refresh rate adapt rather than staying locked at maximum.

Inside sits Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite with 12GB of RAM, a combination rated Excellent for gaming: heavy titles hold up well on high settings, although the phone can grow slightly warm during long sessions without performance falling away. The Leica-branded rear system uses three 50MP cameras, giving you a matched set of sensors rather than one strong lens propped up by fillers, and the 32MP front camera handles selfies and video calls. There is no headphone jack, but you do get NFC, Bluetooth 5.4, USB-C 3.2 and an ultrasonic under-display fingerprint reader.

A 5,240mAh battery pairs with 90W wired charging, so top-ups are measured in minutes rather than hours. It ships on Android 15 with HyperOS 2, and Xiaomi promises four Android upgrades plus security patches running until 2031, with unusually low bloatware for the brand. Choose it if you want maximum speed and long software support in a smaller body; skip it if you prefer a bigger screen for media or need a headphone jack.

software.software_notes: Xiaomi promises 4 Android upgrades and security patches until 2031. HyperOS 2 on the flagship is clean and smooth with almost no bloatware.

gaming.gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 8 Elite is among the fastest chips in the world — heavy games will run smoothly even on high settings. It may get slightly warm during long gaming sessions, but performance stays strong.

overview:

overview:

That combination places it well above basic daily use, covering demanding apps without strain.

Gaming earns an Excellent rating, with heavy games running smoothly on high settings and the 120Hz screen making play feel more responsive. Cameras consist of a 48MP wide lens with sensor-shift OIS plus a 48MP ultrawide, while the front camera is 18MP. overview:

It also brings IP68 and IP69 dust and water resistance and 50W wireless charging, extras most rivals here omit. OxygenOS 15 on Android 15 is described as clean, fast and ad-free with low bloatware, and OnePlus promises four Android upgrades up to Android 19 plus six years of security patches.

The 6.82-inch LTPO AMOLED screen runs at 120Hz with a sharp 1440x3168 resolution, and connectivity includes USB-C 3.2, NFC and Bluetooth 5.4, though no headphone jack. Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite on a 3nm process earns an Excellent gaming rating, handling heavy games smoothly on high settings, helped by a 6,000mAh battery, 100W wired charging and cooling suited to long sessions, according to its gaming notes.

All three rear cameras use 50MP sensors: a wide lens with OIS and Hasselblad branding, an ultrawide, and a periscope telephoto offering 3x zoom, with a 32MP front camera. Buy it for top-end speed, zoom and durability; skip it if the budget is tighter or wireless charging and water resistance hold no value for you.

overview:

The Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, a flagship chip built on 4nm, gives the phone an Excellent gaming rating, with any game expected to run smoothly on high settings. A 6,000mAh battery and 80W charging support those long sessions without painfully slow refills.

Camera duties fall to a 50MP wide sensor with OIS, a 50MP telephoto with 2x zoom and an 8MP ultrawide, while selfies are handled by a 16MP unit that is modest on paper beside the rear set. overview:
Honor pitches the 400 around its camera and long software support, and in Pakistan it appears at a market price of Rs 194,999 via Softliee for the 8GB and 256GB variant. The 6.55-inch AMOLED panel has a 1264x2736 resolution and 120Hz refresh rate, so it should look considerably sharper and more fluid than LCD rivals. An under-display optical fingerprint reader, 5G, NFC and Bluetooth 5.4 are all included, though there is no headphone jack. The body also carries IP66 dust and water resistance according to the notes.

Inside is Qualcomm's Snapdragon 7 Gen 3 on a 4nm process, rated Very good for gaming, with PUBG expected to run smoothly on medium settings despite this being presented mainly as a camera phone. That camera headline is a 200MP wide rear sensor with OIS, joined by a 12MP ultrawide, while selfies use a notably high-resolution 50MP front camera. There is no telephoto lens listed, so zoom relies on the main sensor rather than dedicated optical hardware.

A 6,000mAh battery with 80W charging provides both a large capacity and rapid top-ups. Software is a major strength: Android 15 with MagicOS 9, low bloatware, and an official promise of six years of Android OS and security updates. It fits buyers who want a high-resolution main camera, an AMOLED screen and unusually long support. Those who need optical zoom or a headphone jack will not find either here.

overview:
Positioned as a battery and durability phone rather than a gaming specialist, the Honor X9c carries a market price of Rs 99,999 for 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, with the notes describing that figure as a last-listed price after a retailer tagged it discontinued. Up front is a 6.78-inch AMOLED display at 1224x2700 resolution and 120Hz, which should deliver crisp text and fluid motion. It includes 5G, NFC, Bluetooth 5.1 and an under-display optical fingerprint reader, without a headphone jack. IP65M rating and SGS drop-resistance certification are also noted.

The Snapdragon 6 Gen 1 (4nm) powers the phone and earns a Good gaming rating, with PUBG said to run fine on medium settings, even though gaming is not its main purpose. Camera hardware is a 108MP wide rear lens with OIS plus a 5MP ultrawide, and a 16MP front camera. That gives stabilised main-camera shooting and a basic wide option, but no telephoto lens for proper zoom work.

A 6,600mAh battery with 66W charging is well above average in capacity and should refill at a healthy pace. Software starts at Android 14 with MagicOS 8, low bloatware is reported, and there is no official update promise for this X-series model. It makes sense for buyers who value battery, toughness and a high-resolution AMOLED screen. Heavy gamers or anyone prioritising a published long-term update plan should choose differently.

Instead of AMOLED you get a 6.8-inch TFT LCD at 1080x2412 resolution with a 120Hz refresh rate, so motion stays fluid even if contrast is not AMOLED-level. It is a 5G phone with NFC, Bluetooth 5.3, a side-mounted fingerprint reader and no headphone jack, and it also supports 5W reverse wired charging.

MediaTek's Dimensity 7025 Ultra on a 6nm process is in charge, rated Good overall, although the notes caution that PUBG is best kept to low-medium settings and the chip is a bit weak for heavy games. The rear system pairs the 108MP wide camera with a 5MP ultrawide, and selfies are handled by a 16MP camera. No OIS or telephoto is listed for this Smart variant, which limits stabilisation and zoom compared with the standard X9c.

Battery capacity stands at 5,800mAh with 35W charging, a solid size but a slower refill rate than its sibling offers. It launched on Android 14 with MagicOS 8, low bloatware is noted, and Honor has made no official update promise for this model. Choose it for generous storage, 5G and a high pixel-count main camera at a lower cost. Leave it if you want an AMOLED screen, OIS or stronger gaming headroom.

overview:

The notes add IP68 and IP69K dust and water resistance, 5G support, NFC and Bluetooth 5.2, but no headphone jack.

Processing comes from the Snapdragon 6 Gen 4 on a 4nm process, rated Good for gaming, with PUBG described as smooth on medium settings. The record also points out that the huge battery allows long gaming sessions away from a charger. Rear cameras consist of a 108MP wide lens with OIS and a small 5MP ultrawide, while the front camera is 16MP. There is no telephoto option, and the ultrawide resolution is modest compared with the main sensor.

Battery capacity is the standout specification at 8,300mAh, far above most phones in this list, with 66W charging and support for 7.5W reverse wired charging. It ships on Android 15 with MagicOS 9 and low bloatware, but Honor has published no update promise for this model. Buy it for maximum endurance, a big AMOLED display and strong water resistance. Skip it if camera versatility or guaranteed update years matter more.

overview:
Anyone considering the Huawei Nova 13 at its market price of Rs 112,800 from PriceUpdate.com.pk should start with the software caveat in the record. It runs HarmonyOS 4.2, presented globally as EMUI 14.2, with no Google Play services at all, meaning no Play Store or Google apps and Huawei's AppGallery instead. The hardware underneath that compromise is strong, centred on 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage for this variant.

The display is a 6.7-inch OLED at 1084x2412 with a 120Hz refresh rate, giving the size and smoothness expected at this level. Huawei's Kirin 8000, a 7nm chip, powers the phone, and the gaming verdict is labelled Good, with smooth high-setting play in PUBG and BGMI and only the heaviest titles needing a small step down from maximum. Bloatware is rated low, though Huawei publishes no promise for how many years of updates the phone will receive.

Rear photography pairs a 50MP wide camera with an 8MP ultrawide, so group and landscape shots are covered but there is no telephoto reach, while the 60MP front camera is the standout for selfie detail. The 5,000mAh battery charges at a very fast 100W and also offers 5W reverse wired charging. Choose it if you accept the AppGallery-only life and value charging speed and selfies; skip it entirely if your apps depend on Google services.
notes: Price is for the 12GB/256GB variant. No Google Mobile Services (uses Huawei AppGallery). Also supports 5W reverse wired charging.

software.software_notes: Huawei publishes no update-year promise. Runs EMUI 14.2 (HarmonyOS-based) with NO Google Play services — no Play Store, no Google apps; Huawei's AppGallery only. Clean software otherwise.

gaming.gaming_notes: With the Kirin 8000 and 12GB RAM, expect smooth high-setting gameplay in PUBG/BGMI; only the heaviest titles need a small step down from max.

overview:

Its 6.76-inch LTPO OLED panel runs at 120Hz with a sharp 2776x1224 resolution, and an optical fingerprint sensor sits beneath the glass. Powering the phone is the HiSilicon Kirin 8000, built on a 7nm process, with 5G connectivity, NFC and Bluetooth 5.2, though the USB-C port is only version 2.0 and there is no headphone jack.

Photography is the centrepiece: a 50MP main camera offers a variable f/1.4-4.0 aperture and OIS, joined by a 12MP 3x telephoto and an 8MP ultrawide, while the front pairing combines 60MP with an 8MP portrait camera. A 5,000mAh battery is matched with very fast 100W charging, so top-ups should take little time. This handset suits camera-focused buyers who can live entirely outside Google's ecosystem, while anyone dependent on the Play Store, Google apps or an official local launch should steer clear.

overview:
October 2024's Galaxy A16 5G sells at a market price of Rs 69,999 according to dailytechprice listings, which cover both 4GB/128GB and 8GB/256GB variants. The display is a 6.7-inch Super AMOLED running at 90Hz, with a side-mounted fingerprint reader.

The standout commitment is software: six years of OS updates and six years of security updates for One UI 6.1 on Android 14, a promise that far outlasts most phones at this price. Samsung's duplicate apps are preinstalled, bloatware is medium, and the system itself carries no ads.

Camera hardware is a 50MP main lens with 5MP and 2MP supporting units and a 13MP front camera; no optical stabilisation is listed, so the main sensor works unaided in dimmer light and the small companions add minimal range. The 5,000mAh battery supports 25W charging. NFC is included, Bluetooth is 5.3, and there is no headphone jack. It is a longevity-first 5G option for patient buyers; performance hunters will find the chipset modest.

overview:
Samsung has not officially launched the Galaxy A06 5G in Pakistan, so units here are grey or imported stock, with a market price of around Rs 30,700 reported by bestmobile.pk. This is a different handset from the 4G Galaxy A06: it runs a MediaTek Dimensity 6300 chip and brings 5G to a budget price point. The listed configuration pairs 4GB of RAM with 64GB of storage, plus a side-mounted fingerprint reader, a headphone jack and Bluetooth 5.3, though NFC is absent.

The 6.7-inch PLS LCD is an HD+ panel, so text and video will not look as crisp as on a Full HD screen, but its 90Hz refresh rate does make scrolling feel a step smoother than a basic display. Performance is rated Average for gaming: the Dimensity 6300 handles light games comfortably, yet PUBG can lag once settings get heavy. The rear camera pairs a 50MP main sensor with a 2MP secondary lens, which is a setup for everyday snaps rather than zoom or wide-angle work, and the 8MP front camera covers routine selfies and video calls.

A 5,000mAh battery with 25W charging keeps things simple, and software is a genuine strength: Android 15 with One UI 7, no ads in the system, and four years of OS plus four years of security updates promised, even though Samsung's duplicate apps come preinstalled. Pick it for an affordable route into 5G with long support; skip it if you need a sharp display, strong gaming or an official local launch.

overview:
With an official Samsung Pakistan price of Rs 94,999, the Galaxy A26 5G undercuts several newer rivals despite launching in March 2025 and reaching Pakistan that April — although PriceOye now shows the model as discontinued, so availability may vary by seller. Its 6.7-inch Super AMOLED screen runs at 120Hz and houses an optical in-display fingerprint reader, and 5G, NFC and Bluetooth 5.3 round out the connectivity list.

The Exynos 1380, built on 5nm, earns a good gaming rating: PUBG and BGMI play smoothly on this hardware, with only slight warmth reported during very long sessions. Memory is 8GB of RAM with 256GB of storage. Software support is a major selling point, with six years of OS updates and six years of security patches promised for One UI 7 over Android 15, even if Samsung's own duplicate apps come preinstalled and bloatware sits at a medium level.

At the back, a 50MP camera with optical stabilisation leads a trio completed by 8MP and 2MP lenses, and selfies are handled by 13MP. The main camera is clearly the serious tool of the three rear units. Power comes from a 5,000mAh battery charging at 25W, which is functional rather than fast. There is no headphone jack. It suits buyers who value a smooth display, stabilised main camera and long update runway — provided you can still find one in stock.

overview:

The display grows slightly to 6.7 inches, and Android 15 comes out of the box with Samsung's long update runway ahead of it.

Cameras stay familiar — a 50MP OIS main, 8MP ultrawide and 5MP macro, with a 12MP front camera — and storage is a generous 256GB with 8GB RAM. At the same Rs 119,999 as the A35, the A36 is the one to buy new: faster charging, a newer chip and a longer support life ahead of it.

overview:
The Galaxy A56 5G is the A-series all-rounder of its year: Exynos 1580 performance, a 50MP OIS main camera with a proper 12MP ultrawide beside it, and 45W charging that finally matches the phone's ambitions. Android 15 out of the box and Samsung's update policy give it a long useful life.

At Rs 137,999 it costs Rs 18,000 more than the A36, and the differences are the chip, the better ultrawide and the more refined overall package. The 6.7-inch display, 5,000mAh battery, 8GB RAM, 256GB storage and 12MP selfie camera are shared ground. If your budget stops below the A57, the A56 is the balanced buy — nothing about it is the best in class, but nothing is weak either.

overview:
The Infinix Note 60 Ultra's headline feature is one no rival in its class offers: two-way satellite communication. Through Thuraya's GEO satellite network — covering around 120 countries across Asia, Europe and Africa — it can make and receive real satellite voice calls and exchange two-way SMS in places with no mobile signal at all, which Infinix says makes it the first commercially available smartphone with dual-way satellite calling across multiple countries. For travellers, trekkers, remote-area workers and emergencies, that is a genuine safety net rather than a gimmick. It runs on a separate Thuraya SIM at paid satellite rates (higher than normal calls), and satellite mode switches off Wi-Fi, mobile data and the camera while connected — it provides calls and texts only, not satellite internet.

Beyond the satellite link, this is a full flagship-grade package. Battery capacity is 7,000mAh — well above average, and the kind of size that can stretch to two days for lighter users — and 100W charging (plus 50W wireless charging) means top-ups are genuinely quick when you are in a hurry.

On the software side it runs Android 16 with XOS 16. It is aimed at buyers who want premium features — and a level of off-grid connectivity nothing else at this price offers — without paying full flagship money. In Pakistan it is listed at Rs 199,999 (official price, checked 2026-09-30) — confirm the final price, variant and warranty with the seller before paying. Thuraya coverage and service availability vary by country, so check Thuraya's coverage for your area before relying on the satellite feature.

That jump changes its value . Extras in the record include IP64 protection, dual speakers, FM radio, OTG support and a headphone jack, though NFC is absent and there is no 5G.

The 6.67-inch IPS LCD refreshes at 120Hz, unusually fast for an entry phone, which helps the interface feel responsive even if the underlying hardware is modest. That hardware is a Unisoc T7250 with 4GB of RAM, and gaming is rated weak: this is a phone for light games and daily tasks, not demanding titles. Android 15 with HiOS 15 is current software for the class, bloatware is rated medium, and Tecno has published no update promise for the model.

A single 13MP rear camera with PDAF handles photography, supported by an 8MP front camera; with no secondary rear lens listed, zoom and wide shots are simply not part of the package. The 5,000mAh battery should cover routine daily use, and 15W charging is a small step above the slowest 10W standard in this segment. A side-mounted fingerprint reader adds convenient security. It makes sense for first-time smartphone buyers who want a big, smooth screen, recent Android and basic durability, but gamers and anyone needing generous storage should pass.

overview:

Choose it for telephoto photography, sustained gaming and wireless charging; buyers who rank a guaranteed multi-year update policy above camera reach may prefer a rival that publishes one.

overview:

Its specification is modest today: 3GB of RAM, 32GB of storage, a rear-mounted fingerprint reader, NFC and a headphone jack. It launched on Android 8.1 Oreo as part of Android One, and no update figures are published in the record.

Its 5.84-inch IPS LCD is one of its better features, offering HDR10 and a 1080x2280 resolution protected by Gorilla Glass 3, which makes it a sharp, compact screen for video and reading. The Snapdragon 636 chipset is rated average for gaming in the record, but the accompanying notes are blunt: only the lightest games run well, and anything with heavy 3D graphics is likely to feel frustrating and laggy. This is hardware for messaging, browsing and media rather than play.

At the back, a 12MP wide camera with dual pixel PDAF and an f/1.8 aperture is joined by a 5MP depth sensor, while selfies use an 8MP camera; there is no stabilisation, ultrawide or telephoto in the list. The battery is just 3,060mAh, small even for a compact phone, with 18W charging to compensate somewhat through quicker top-ups. It may appeal if you find one cheaply and want a small phone with a good screen, but limited storage, an ageing processor and that small battery make newer budget phones the safer buy.
notes: Discontinued; no current Pakistan price found

gaming.gaming_notes: Only the lightest games will run well on the Snapdragon 636; anything 3D-heavy is likely to be a frustrating, laggy experience.

overview:
PriceOye lists the Nokia 6.1 Plus at a market price of Rs 28,799, but the record is clear that the model is discontinued in Pakistan and that figure is a last-updated price with no current retail availability. Dating back to 2018, it appeals mainly to someone who finds a clean used unit and prefers a smaller phone over today's oversized designs.

At 5.8 inches, its IPS LCD is compact by modern standards, yet its 1080x2280 Full HD+ resolution makes it sharper on paper than many newer budget screens. Performance comes from a Snapdragon 636 with 4GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, enough for essentials first, with gaming restricted to simple, undemanding titles according to the record's average rating. Software starts from Android 8.1 Oreo on Android One, and the phone keeps a headphone jack, USB Type-C, Bluetooth 5.0 and a rear fingerprint reader, though NFC is missing.

Camera hardware comprises a 16MP main sensor with PDAF and a 5MP depth companion, so portraits get depth assistance but there is no ultrawide or telephoto option, while the 16MP front camera matches the rear unit's resolution. Battery capacity is just 3,060mAh, partly offset by 18W charging that is quicker than the 10W setups on many old Nokias. Buy it only as an inexpensive compact for calls, browsing and media; skip it if battery endurance, modern apps at speed or camera flexibility matter.

overview:
Curved glass and a compact footprint define this 2018 Nokia, at a market price of Rs 94,000 via HamariWeb even though it is discontinued, with no current Pakistan price found. Up front sits a 5.5-inch curved pOLED panel at sharp 1440x2560 QHD resolution behind Gorilla Glass 5. There is no headphone jack, though NFC, Bluetooth 5.0 and USB Type-C 3.0 are present, and unlocking is handled by a rear-mounted fingerprint sensor.

Inside, a Snapdragon 835 on a 10nm process works with 6GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. The record credits that former flagship chip with solid PUBG Mobile play and competence in mid-tier titles, while warning it is not suited to modern games at maximum settings. Its rear pair combines a 12MP wide camera with dual pixel PDAF and f/1.8 aperture alongside a 13MP telephoto offering 2x optical zoom, a genuinely useful extra most phones here lack. Selfies, by contrast, rely on only a 5MP front camera. Power comes from a small 3,260mAh cell with 18W charging, so heavy users will be reaching for a charger sooner than owners of larger-battery phones.

Software started on Android 8.0 Oreo under Android One, with no published update promise listed, which matters at this age. Consider it only if the curved QHD screen, optical zoom and compact premium build appeal to you as a niche, older flagship. Most buyers should look elsewhere for a bigger battery, a stronger selfie camera, 5G, or any certainty about ongoing support and present-day availability.
notes: Discontinued; no current Pakistan price found

gaming.gaming_notes: Snapdragon 835 flagship — solid for PUBG Mobile and mid-tier titles; not for max-settings modern games.

overview:

overview:
Realme's Note 60x covers the essentials and little more, with a market price of Rs 33,999 recorded for the small 3GB RAM and 64GB storage variant, and other variants with more memory listed at higher prices. It brings some durability thinking to the segment, with IP54 protection, ArmorShell construction and reinforced glass noted in the record, plus a dedicated microSD slot for expanding that limited storage. There is no NFC, no 5G, and notably no fingerprint sensor at all.

The display is a 6.74-inch IPS LCD at HD+ resolution, 720x1600, with a 90Hz refresh rate; motion looks smoother than basic panels, but sharpness is limited by the resolution, which shows on text and video detail. A Unisoc Tiger T612 processor powers the phone, and gaming is rated weak: it is strictly for basic use, with simple, light titles running best. Android 14 with realme UI 5.0 is the software, and no update support is published.

Cameras are minimal: an 8MP main camera with an auxiliary lens at the back and a 5MP front camera, enough for casual records of moments rather than quality photography, with no wide, zoom or stabilisation features listed. The 5,000mAh battery is a solid size for such modest hardware, although 10W charging means slow refills. It suits someone upgrading from a feature phone or needing a tough, simple second handset; the lack of fingerprint security, low RAM and weak cameras make it hard to recommend as a primary phone for most people.

overview:
With an official price of Rs 389,999, the Galaxy S23 Ultra undercuts several newer flagships while keeping a specification sheet that still reads as heavyweight. Its 6.8-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X screen runs at 120Hz with HDR10+ and a 3088 x 1440 resolution, among the sharpest listed here. The Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for Galaxy, in an overclocked-GPU form according to the gaming notes, works alongside 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.

Those gaming notes call the device a monster for play, pointing to the huge display, stereo speakers and 5,000mAh battery as a complete flagship gaming package. Photography is led by a 200MP rear camera, supported by 12MP, 10MP and 10MP companions, so the hardware covers far more ground than the 12MP front camera alone would suggest. Charging reaches 45W, biometrics use an ultrasonic under-display fingerprint sensor, and the phone includes 5G, NFC, Bluetooth 5.3 and USB Type-C 3.2 with no headphone jack.

It launched on Android 13 with One UI 5.1, and Samsung's stated support in the record is four years of OS updates plus five years of security updates. This is a strong pick for buyers who want the big-screen Ultra experience and a 200MP-led camera system without paying the newest model's price. Skip it if you prefer a lighter phone or want the longest possible update runway.

gaming.gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 for Galaxy with its overclocked GPU is a gaming monster. The huge 6.8-inch display, stereo speakers, and 5000mAh battery deliver a true flagship gaming experience.

overview:
Positioned as the more affordable route into Samsung's S23 family, the Galaxy S23 FE has an official price of Rs 204,999 listed by WhatMobile. It arrived in October 2023 running Android 13 and One UI 5.1, with four years of OS updates and five years of security updates promised in its record. Day-to-day hardware includes 5G, NFC, Bluetooth 5.3, USB Type-C 3.2 and an optical in-screen fingerprint reader, but wired headphone users get no 3.5mm port here.

The front is dominated by a 6.4-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X panel at 2340 x 1080, refreshing at 120Hz and supporting HDR10+, so motion looks clean and compatible video gets extra punch. Samsung fits the Exynos 2200, a 4nm chip, alongside 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage — the storage figure is half what some pricier siblings offer. Gaming performance is solid at high settings for popular titles according to the record, although this chip runs warmer than the Snapdragon variants, and the fast display helps gameplay feel responsive.

A 50MP primary camera leads the rear trio, with 8MP and 12MP supporting lenses widening your shooting choices, while a 10MP camera up front covers self-portraits. Battery capacity is 4,500mAh with 25W charging, modest numbers next to rivals offering larger cells or quicker top-ups. It makes sense for Samsung loyalists who value the display and update pledge at this price; heat-conscious heavy gamers and anyone needing lots of built-in storage should look elsewhere.

gaming.gaming_notes: The Exynos 2200 handles popular games well at high settings, though it runs warmer than the Snapdragon variants. The 120Hz display keeps gameplay smooth for most titles.

overview:

Its 6.7-inch Dynamic LTPO AMOLED 2X display brings QHD+ resolution of 1440x3120 and a 120Hz refresh rate, a step up in sharpness from FHD+ panels. The gaming notes say the Exynos 2400 with Xclipse 940 graphics handles PUBG Mobile at 120fps on Smooth settings and 60fps at HDR, though sustained loads can produce noticeable heat. Even so, the fluid QHD+ panel keeps gameplay vivid, placing it just below the Ultra as a gaming choice. Rear cameras are listed at 50MP, 12MP and 10MP, with a 12MP front camera, giving a versatile triple setup without the Ultra's 200MP headline sensor. A 4,900mAh battery with 45W charging should suit longer days better than the smaller S24, and unlocking is handled by an ultrasonic under-display fingerprint reader.

It launched on Android 14 with One UI 6.1, and update years are not published in this record. Consider it if you want the larger, sharper screen and bigger battery without stepping up to Ultra pricing. If sustained gaming without heat build-up is your top concern, the Snapdragon-powered alternatives deserve a look first.

gaming.gaming_notes: The Exynos 2400 with Xclipse 940 graphics handles heavy titles like PUBG Mobile at 120fps on Smooth settings and 60fps at HDR, though sustained loads can cause noticeable heat. overview:
The Nokia 2360 Flip is HMD's new clamshell feature phone, launched in the Philippines on 2 November 2026 for seniors and school children who want a phone that behaves like a phone. It pairs a 2.8-inch QVGA main display with a 1.77-inch outer screen for checking callers without opening it, plus a physical keypad, FM radio, a 3.5mm jack and USB Type-C.

Its headline features are safety ones: a dedicated orange SOS button that calls a preset contact and texts up to five more, and Family Assist, which lets a relative manage contacts, volume, reminders and SOS settings remotely by SMS — no data plan needed. Parental controls behind a Family PIN round out the package, and the removable 1450mAh battery is rated for up to 27.5 hours of talk time or 15 days of standby.

With just 4MB of RAM and storage (microSD to 32GB), a QVGA camera and 2G-only connectivity, the 2360 Flip has no apps, no 4G and no social media — deliberately. It is a simplicity-and-safety phone, not a smartphone, and it has no Pakistan launch or price yet.

overview:

overview:

overview:
